novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1 (causal bridge)
novelty_flags.one_line: This is the standard Rosenbaum--Rubin identification bridge and should be background/supporting material rather than counted as a novel result.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 3 and Open-ended Question 1
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Ma, Sant'Anna, Sasaki, and Ura, “Doubly Robust Estimators with Weak Overlap,” arXiv:2304.08974v3 (2026), the closest omitted public theorem text on bias-corrected DR estimation under weak overlap; it is clean-record and does not subsume this kernel.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 1 (causal bridge)
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed equality with the Lebesgue integral needs ass:uniform-design, but that assumption is neither stated in the proposition nor listed among its dependencies.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 2 (raw projection failure)
soundness_flags.one_line: “Raw second-order pair correction” and “correct pilots” are not defined, and the kernel normalization/cross-fitting convention needed to make the displayed expectation shift meaningful is absent.

soundness_flags.label: ass:boundary-extension
soundness_flags.one_line: Given ass:outcome-regression-law and mu_1 in the full-cube Hölder class, continuity already fixes its boundary trace; the separate boundary-extension condition is redundant.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The primary article states that adjustment on the propensity score is sufficient to remove bias from observed covariates in observational causal-effect studies.
The article establishes irregularity from unbounded inverse weights and includes an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.

source_verification_receipts.version: Electronic Journal of Statistics 10(2), 2016, pp. 3752-3774; corroborated against arXiv:1511.04144
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work studies the Huber mixture experiment, gives a robust testing construction, and uses a modulus-of-continuity lower-bound term.
The article develops U-statistics based on higher-order influence functions for nonparametric and semiparametric functional estimation.
The article proposes density-power IPW/DR extensions for outlier resistance and states that naive DR robustification needs bias correction to retain double robustness.
The paper gives clean-model ATE minimax lower bounds and a higher-order/doubly robust estimator under hybrid smoothness and structure-agnostic conditions.
The paper implements bias-corrected smooth trimming for limited-overlap ATE estimation with parametric propensity fitting and asymptotic inference.
The omitted preprint develops trimming and bias-corrected doubly robust estimators for weak overlap under clean records; it does not posit arbitrary full-record Huber contamination.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Ma--Sant'Anna--Sasaki--Ura as the nearest clean weak-overlap comparator and state explicitly why its trimming/bias correction does not handle replacement of X and A.

Repair the causal bridge by conditioning it on the uniform design, and define the raw projected pair statistic, pilot construction, kernel normalization, and sample-splitting convention before retaining the contamination diagnostic.

After the Lipschitz calibration, solve a second nontrivial higher-dimensional or noninteger-smoothness slice with a same-experiment converse to make the general interaction question less dependent on one calibration case.

recommended_next_step: Revise the three local defects and survey gap, then advance the repaired full-frontier angle to Stage 0 as a field-tier minimax problem.
